title: Evidence remains mixed across the two illustrative cohorts
summary: Cohort A observed the target behavior in 74 of 200 participants; cohort B observed it in 62 of 200. Because sample composition and observation windows differed, comparison is limited and the synthesis can only identify what remains unresolved.

sections.title: Both cohorts observed the behavior, but design differences limit comparison
paragraphs: Both studies observed the target behavior, yet their sample composition and observation windows differed. Adding the counts would make distinct research questions look like one estimate.
The evidence can prioritize the next comparison, but it cannot establish a causal intervention effect or a population-wide effect size.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Both cohorts observed the target behavior, but their different windows prevent pooling.
figures.accessibleDescription: In illustrative cohorts with different sample composition and observation windows, cohort A observed the target behavior in 74 of 200 participants over 14 days, while cohort B observed it in 62 of 200 participants over 30 days. The values are not pooled.

quotations.text: The two cohorts do not estimate the same effect.
quotations.originalText: 두 코호트는 같은 효과를 추정하지 않는다.

limitations: All numbers are illustrative and exist only to exercise the report contract.
Observation windows and sample composition differ, so no pooled effect was calculated.
Unmeasured confounding prevents a causal-strength judgment.

claims.text: The target behavior was observed in both cohorts.
claims.qualificationText: Illustrative cohorts with different designs and windows

claims.text: The current evidence cannot establish a pooled causal effect.
claims.qualificationText: No pooled estimate and no causal interpretation
